metadata.title: Perceived teacher autonomy support for adolescents' reading achievement: The mediation roles of control-value appraisals and emotions

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the PISA 2018 reading assessment subset for China (15-year-olds) and analyzes a student-level questionnaire and reading achievement outcome. In the Methods section, the authors state that “student weights were calculated among the measures examined,” but they do not report the specific weight variable name or whether complex survey replicate weights were applied. Because the analysis is conducted with lavaan (MLR) for a multiple mediation model rather than a survey-weighted ML pipeline, the manuscript provides limited transparency on how PISA’s complex sampling design was incorporated into standard errors and model fit. For replication, analysts should use the official PISA student sampling weights (and replicate weights if available) corresponding to the PISA 2018 China reading dataset and the PVREAD plausible value used (PV1 reading), and then re-estimate the mediation model under the same weighting scheme.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2018 secondary dataset released in December 2019, restricting to the China subset and the reading achievement domain. The analytic outcome uses reading achievement measured with PV1 reading (PVREAD). The study imputes missing data across the entire dataset using the EM algorithm before estimating the multiple serial mediation model; no additional grade/school-type restrictions are reported beyond the PISA 15-year-old target population.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Multiple serial mediation (lavaan MLR). Model fit: CFI=0.990, TLI=0.947, RMSEA=0.078, SRMR=0.045. Direct effect: AUTOSUP→PVREAD B=2.790 (SE=1.120, p<0.05). Indirect effects: AUTOSUP→APPRAISALS→PVREAD B=-2.280 (SE=0.868, p<0.05); AUTOSUP→JOYREAD→PVREAD B=1.660 (SE=0.387, p<0.001); AUTOSUP→APPRAISALS→JOYREAD→PVREAD B=7.270 (SE=0.655, p<0.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (China, 15-year-olds; PV1 reading), the study leveraged teacher autonomy support, socioeconomic status (ESCS), gender, reading self-efficacy, meaning in life, and reading enjoyment to predict reading achievement, finding that teacher autonomy support had a positive direct association with reading achievement (B=2.790) and also an indirect positive pathway through reading enjoyment (B=1.660). It further found that the serial pathway through control-value appraisals (self-efficacy and meaning in life) to reading achievement was negative (B=-2.280) while the full serial chain through appraisals and then enjoyment to achievement was positive (B=7.270). This indicates that autonomy-supportive teaching may improve reading outcomes primarily by fostering reading enjoyment, while the role of motivational appraisals is context-dependent and may require the emotional pathway to translate into achievement gains.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzed a China subset of PISA 2018 reading for 15-year-old students (n=12,058) and modeled reading achievement using PV1 reading, normalized to an OECD scale (mean 500, SD 100). The authors estimated a serial multiple mediation model in R (lavaan) with maximum likelihood estimation with robust standard errors (MLR), reporting acceptable fit (CFI=0.990, TLI=0.947, RMSEA=0.078, SRMR=0.045). Teacher autonomy support showed a positive direct effect on reading achievement (B=2.790, p<0.05) and a significant positive indirect effect via reading enjoyment (B=1.660, p<0.001). In contrast, the indirect path through control-value appraisals alone was negative (B=-2.280, p<0.05), while the full serial chain through appraisals and then enjoyment to achievement was positive (B=7.270, p<0.001). Limitations include cross-sectional mediation assumptions, self-report measures for autonomy support and emotions, and limited reporting of how PISA complex sampling weights were applied in the mediation estimation.
